sections.overview: Pseudantechinus mimulus is a recognized dasyurid species from northern Australia.
sections.identification: It resembles P. bilarni and P. macdonnellensis; the 2024 study cautions that camera-trap images may not reliably separate them.
sections.habitat: Confirmed records are from rocky outcrops in Queensland and the Northern Territory.
sections.diet: The reviewed distribution study does not establish a species-specific prey list.
sections.behavior: Movements are poorly known; one male moved about 2 km in 24 h.
sections.reproduction: Reproductive biology is not detailed in the study reviewed here.
sections.ecology: In the Mount Isa Inlier it uses varied rocky outcrops; habitat links elsewhere remain uncertain.
sections.conservation: The 2024 authors report an IUCN Near Threatened category; they recommend Data Deficient for Australian assessment pending more data.
